question: A newspaper offered 2.1 million readers a trial that renewed automatically or one that simply ended. Which left more subscribers two years later?
answer: The trial that simply ended. Miller, Sahni and Strulov-Shlain found far more of those on auto-renewal kept paying straight after the trial than on the other offer. But readers wary of forgetting shunned it: sign-ups fell 24%, and two years on the paper had about 10% fewer subscribers. Readers saw the trap coming.
move: Judge a tactic by everyone it reached, not only by those who said yes.
ask: Which tactic am I judging by those who said yes and ignoring everyone it reached?
trap: Judging auto-renewal only by the readers who accepted it.
reference: Miller, Sahni & Strulov-Shlain, Sophisticated Consumers with Inertia: Long-Term Implications from a Large-Scale Field Experiment, Stanford GSB Working Paper, 2022
